name: Evaluation Datasets
blurb: Benchmarks and test sets, and what each actually measures.

items.note: Grade-school math word problems; the standard arithmetic-reasoning test
Science exam questions in easy and challenge splits
57-subject knowledge exam; the most-cited general capability benchmark
The successor suite to GLUE for language understanding
Commonsense sentence completion designed to be adversarial to models
164 hand-written programming problems; the original code-generation benchmark
The harder ten-choice successor as frontier models saturated MMLU
Graduate-level science questions that resist search; gated to keep answers out of training data

reading.body:
Nine benchmarks make up this collection, and their own descriptions trace a specific arc, MMLU-Pro is explicitly named as the harder successor built after frontier models saturated the original MMLU, the most downloaded general-capability benchmark in this set at 606,503 downloads.

GSM8K, the grade-school math word problem set, is the most downloaded benchmark overall at 1,167,043 downloads, ahead of AI2 ARC's science exam questions at 683,123 and MMLU itself. GPQA, a graduate-level science benchmark with only 121,507 downloads, the lowest in this collection, is described as deliberately gated to keep its answers out of training data, a direct defense against the same contamination problem that pushed MMLU-Pro's creation, and a different design choice than every other benchmark in this set, none of which are marked gated.

HellaSwag is described as commonsense sentence completion designed to be adversarial to models, and HumanEval, the original code-generation benchmark, is specified as exactly 164 hand-written programming problems, a fixed and small set relative to the hundreds of thousands of downloads it has accumulated, showing that a benchmark's size and its adoption are unrelated in this data.
